by: midtown.html (RULING FV): the move library, written out from MIDTOWN.actors.moves — remake it after changing a move
note: counts: a loop's length in beats (once: played once over them, then held). midtown.html dances them; blocking.html offers them (its Dance button); tools/blocking-merge.py accepts these names. Each is described, with its source, in docs/hamilton-dance-moves.md.

step-touch.desc: step right, touch left beside it, step left, touch right

grapevine.desc: to the right: side, behind, side, touch; then back to the left

box-step.desc: right foot forward, left crosses over, right back, left to the side: a square

sway.desc: her weight side to side, arms floating

bounce.desc: a pulse: the knees dip on every beat (also "pulse")

clap.desc: the hands meet in front of her chest on every beat

point.desc: the right arm points up and out on 1, holds, comes down on 4

lunge.desc: the right foot forward into a lunge on 1, held, back on 4

kneel.desc: down onto the right knee over two counts, and stay there

rise.desc: up from a kneel to standing tall, the arms opening up and out

spin-quarter.desc: a quarter turn to her left on the spot (mirror: to the right)

spin-half.desc: a half turn on the spot

spin-full.desc: a full turn on the spot, arms in, then out

reach-up.desc: both arms up over her head on 1, up on her toes, held

arm-sweep.desc: the right arm sweeps from low across her up to high on the right, the body turning with it

salute.desc: the right hand to her brow, standing tall, held

bow.desc: a bow from the waist: down by 2, held, up by 4; one hand across her, one behind

curtsy.desc: the right foot slides behind, the knees dip, a little bow; the hands out as if holding a skirt

freeze.desc: she holds the pose she had on its first count, still as a statue

slow-walk.desc: the walk in slow motion on the spot — one stride every four counts (reverse: the "rewind", the walk run backwards)

stomp.desc: a knee up on the "and", stamped down on the beat; right then left

jump.desc: down on 1, up in the air on the "and", landing on 2

kick.desc: a kick forward with the right leg, then the left

two-step.desc: the hip-hop two-step: out to the side and together, right then left, a bounce on every beat

march.desc: marching on the spot: the knees up in turn, the arms swinging straight

pulse.desc: a pulse: the knees dip on every beat (also "pulse")

my-shot.desc: "Just like my country I'm young, scrappy and hungry, and I'm not throwing away my shot": second position, reach out to the people, hand to the heart, the hand flicks out, the boxer's groove, the roundhouse punch, the shot snapped down

legacy.desc: the My Shot phrase as it returns at "Legacy" at the end of the show: the same, but the shot is thrown UP

imagine-death.desc: Yorktown, "I imagined death so much it feels more like a memory": a hand behind the head, a hand across the chest, chin up; a knee up and a punch for "on my feet, enemy ahead of me"; arms crossed for "if this is the end of me"

command.desc: Yorktown, "weapon in my hand, a command, and boom": the rifle overhead, the forearm across the face, fists up and shoulders squared, the hands on the epaulets

heartbeat.desc: Yorktown, thinking of Eliza: a contraction on each "boom" of the heartbeat, then a point to the head

hiphop-march.desc: Yorktown, "we gotta go, we gotta get the job done": a hip-hop step like a march — out with the arms wide, the shoulders brushed off, a foot pushed out, down

musket.desc: firing a musket that weighs 35 pounds: a wide stance, the back used, aim, and the recoil through the whole body on the beat

hoist.desc: Hurricane: what she carries hoisted overhead, arms straight up, like the storm lifting it (a carried prop rises with her hands)

upside-down.desc: Yorktown, "the world turned upside down": furniture lifted overhead and turned upside down, held there (a carried prop flips over)

shimmy.desc: The Room Where It Happens: Burr's ego mocking him — the Fosse-like upper-body shimmy, knees bent and turned in, jazz hands, the head cocked

jazz-roll.desc: The Room Where It Happens' "ooey-gooey jazz": a slow hip roll, the shoulders sliding against it, the hands drifting up and down

crawl-back.desc: Hurricane, the "cockroaches": on hands and knees, crawling backward in slow motion (travelling, she turns her back to her path, so she crawls backward along it)

gavotte.desc: Helpless / Satisfied: the formal court dance — upright, up on the toes, one palm raised to her partner's, step and close each way (mirror her partner)

grind.desc: Helpless: twenty seconds after the palms touched, "they want to grind" — the hips rolling low, the arms round a partner

equals.desc: The Schuyler Sisters, "…that all men are created equal": the forearms held level one above the other in front of her — an equals sign

work.desc: The Schuyler Sisters, "…include women in the sequel. Work!": a hand up (the two fingers), the other on the hip, the hip popped

wall-ooze.desc: The Reynolds Pamphlet, round Angelica: slow motion into an invisible wall, the hit, then oozing down and out of it

bojangles.desc: Fred Astaire's "Bojangles of Harlem" (one in front, many behind doing the same): a heel dig forward each beat, the arms swinging, a clap on the "and" of 2

bullet.desc: The World Was Wide Enough, the Bullet: walking in slow motion, one arm out ahead carrying the bullet toward him (one stride every four counts; the path carries her)

row.desc: the rowers at Hamilton's death (and the duellists' boats): kneeling, a long stroke — reach forward, pull to the chest, lean back, recover

rewind.desc: Satisfied's rewind: the slow-motion walk run backwards (the slow walk with reverse); travelling, she turns her back to her path
